reference.source: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine / Kelley's Textbook of Rheumatology
clinicalPearls: Presents with arthralgia, myalgia, fever, serositis and constitutional symptoms after weeks to months of exposure to a culprit drug
Classic culprits include procainamide and hydralazine (highest risk), and also isoniazid, minocycline, quinidine and certain anticonvulsants
Anti-histone antibodies are characteristically positive, while anti-dsDNA antibodies are usually absent (a helpful contrast with idiopathic systemic lupus)
Renal and central nervous system involvement are uncommon compared with idiopathic lupus
Anti-TNF and other biologic agents cause a distinct form that may include anti-dsDNA positivity and occasional organ involvement
Slow acetylator status increases susceptibility to hydralazine- and procainamide-induced disease
The cornerstone of management is withdrawal of the offending drug, with symptoms usually resolving over weeks to months
A short course of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs or corticosteroids may be used for troublesome symptoms during recovery
reference.pathophysiology: Drug-induced lupus is a systemic autoimmune reaction triggered by chronic drug exposure. Several mechanisms are proposed, including drug-induced disruption of central immune tolerance, inhibition of DNA methylation altering T-cell gene expression, and formation of reactive metabolites (often by activated neutrophils or hepatic oxidation) that modify nuclear proteins and break self-tolerance. This drives production of antinuclear antibodies, particularly against the histone-DNA complex, giving the characteristic anti-histone antibody positivity. Slow acetylators accumulate parent drug and are at higher risk with hydralazine and procainamide. Unlike idiopathic disease, immune complex deposition rarely causes significant nephritis, and manifestations typically remit once the drug and its metabolites are cleared.
additionalDifferentials: Other connective tissue diseases (mixed connective tissue disease, undifferentiated)
additionalInvestigations: Antinuclear antibody testing (typically positive, often homogeneous)
Anti-histone antibodies to support the diagnosis
Anti-dsDNA and complement levels to help distinguish from idiopathic lupus
Full blood count for cytopenias and inflammatory markers (ESR/CRP)
Urinalysis and renal function to screen for the rare renal involvement
Chest radiography or echocardiography where serositis is suspected
redFlags: Significant pericardial or pleural effusion causing haemodynamic or respiratory compromise
Renal involvement with proteinuria or an active urinary sediment (uncommon, prompts reassessment)
Persistent or worsening symptoms despite withdrawal of the suspected agent
reference.prognosis: The prognosis is generally excellent; clinical features usually resolve within weeks to months of stopping the culprit drug, though serological abnormalities may persist longer. Serious organ-threatening disease is rare, and permanent sequelae are unusual.
pitfalls: Mistaking drug-induced lupus for idiopathic systemic lupus and committing the patient to long-term immunosuppression
Failing to review the full medication list, including recently started antihypertensives, antiarrhythmics and biologics
Assuming a positive antinuclear antibody alone confirms the diagnosis without the compatible clinical picture
Not appreciating that biologic-induced lupus can behave atypically with anti-dsDNA positivity
references: Kelley and Firestein's Textbook of Rheumatology
management: Withdraw the culprit drug (classically procainamide or hydralazine), the definitive step, after which symptoms usually remit over weeks to months
Relieve arthralgia, myalgia and serositis with non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs
Use a short course of corticosteroids for significant serositis or symptoms not controlled by non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs
Consider hydroxychloroquine for persistent musculoskeletal or cutaneous manifestations
Monitor clinical resolution and manage the uncommon renal or anti-TNF-associated organ involvement as it arises
Document the offending drug, advise avoidance, and reassure that serological abnormalities may persist after clinical recovery
